title: Death cap mushroom
summary: Amanita phalloides is a poisonous mushroom whose amatoxins can cause severe liver injury after ingestion. Toxicity is associated with consuming the mushroom, not with active venom delivery.

title: Amanita phalloides poison
summary: A poisonous mushroom material associated with amatoxins and severe organ toxicity after ingestion. This record does not claim that every mushroom tissue sample has identical toxin concentration.

title: North African fat-tailed scorpion
summary: Androctonus australis is a medically important scorpion that delivers venom through its sting. Human risk varies with species, dose, route, and individual susceptibility.

title: Androctonus australis venom
summary: A scorpion venom containing neuroactive components. Clinical effects depend on exposure and individual susceptibility; this record does not claim a complete composition.

title: Australian box jellyfish
summary: Chironex fleckeri is a box jellyfish whose tentacles contain nematocysts that discharge venom on contact. It is a cnidarian, not a biting or stinging animal with a centralized stinger.

title: Chironex fleckeri venom
summary: A cnidarian venom delivered through nematocyst discharge on tentacle contact. This record avoids assigning a single compound as the complete cause of contact effects.

title: Botulinum neurotoxin-producing bacterium
summary: Clostridium botulinum is an anaerobic, spore-forming bacterium that can produce botulinum neurotoxins. Botulism is the disease caused by exposure to those toxins; the bacterium is not venomous and does not deliver toxin through a bite or sting.

title: Botulinum neurotoxin
summary: Botulinum neurotoxin is the causal toxic material in botulism. This record describes toxin production and exposure without treating the producing bacterium as venomous.

title: Botulinum neurotoxin-producing bacterium exposure mechanism
aliases: Toxin production in a suitable anaerobic context
summary: Under suitable low-oxygen conditions, some Clostridium botulinum strains can produce botulinum neurotoxin.

title: Geography cone snail
summary: Conus geographus is a predatory cone snail that uses a venom apparatus and a harpoon-like radular tooth to deliver a complex venom to prey.

title: Conus geographus venom
summary: A complex marine venom associated with the cone snail's specialized prey-capture apparatus. The complete mixture and individual toxin contributions are not asserted here.

title: Jimsonweed
summary: Datura stramonium is a poisonous plant containing tropane alkaloids that can cause anticholinergic toxicity after ingestion. The plant does not inject venom.

title: Datura stramonium poison
summary: A plant-associated toxic material containing tropane alkaloids such as atropine and scopolamine. Concentration varies among tissues and exposure contexts.

title: Bobbit worm
summary: Eunice aphroditois is a predatory polychaete annelid with large jaws and a documented role in rapid ambush predation. This dossier conservatively represents contact and bite risk without claiming a fully characterized venom composition.

title: Eunice aphroditois oral secretion
summary: This record preserves the distinction between a documented predatory jaw strike and a fully characterized venom. No isolated toxin or clinical effect is asserted.

title: Gila monster
summary: Heloderma suspectum is a venomous lizard that delivers oral gland secretions through grooved teeth during a prolonged bite. It is distinct from snakes and does not inject venom through hollow fangs.

title: Heloderma suspectum venom
summary: An oral venom secretion associated with lower-jaw glands and grooved teeth. This record does not claim that the lizard uses hollow fangs or that one compound explains all effects.

title: Redback spider
summary: Latrodectus hasselti is a venomous spider that uses a web-associated bite to subdue prey and defend itself. Its venom contains neuroactive components associated with latrodectism.

title: Latrodectus hasselti venom
summary: A spider venom containing neuroactive components associated with latrodectism. This record does not assign a complete composition or attribute every clinical outcome to a single compound.

title: Platypus
summary: Ornithorhynchus anatinus is a semi-aquatic monotreme; adult males deliver venom with a hind-ankle spur, making it a distinctive reference organism for venomous mammals.

title: Inland taipan
summary: Oxyuranus microlepidotus is a large Australian elapid whose bite-delivered venom and remote semi-arid ecology provide a reference profile for venomous reptiles.

title: Golden poison frog
summary: Phyllobates terribilis is a poison frog from Colombia whose skin alkaloids make it a useful reference organism for separating passive poison exposure from active venom injection.

title: Phyllobates terribilis skin poison
summary: A skin-associated mixture of defensive alkaloids. Batrachotoxin is a documented component, but evidence about the isolated compound must not be generalized to the complete skin material.

title: Castor bean plant
summary: Ricinus communis is a poisonous plant whose seeds can contain ricin. Toxicity is associated with ingestion or other exposure to plant material, not with venom delivery.

title: Ricinus communis poison
summary: A plant-associated toxic material linked to ricin in castor bean seeds. This record avoids claims about dose, lethality, or exposure outcome beyond the cited toxicological context.

title: Red imported fire ant
summary: Solenopsis invicta is an ant species widely studied for defensive sting behavior, rapid colony recruitment, and ecological impact where established.

title: Solenopsis invicta venom
summary: A biologically active mixture with alkaloid-rich components and protein fractions relevant to allergic responses.

title: Red imported fire ant exposure mechanism
aliases: Persistent local discomfort in some cases
summary: Ant anchors with mandibles and delivers venom through the stinger.

title: Red imported fire ant sting effects
summary: Direct local tissue effects at sting site.

title: Reef stonefish
summary: Synanceia verrucosa is a cryptic reef-associated fish that delivers venom through dorsal spines, providing a reference profile for mechanically triggered fish envenomation.

title: Amatoxins
summary: This record keeps amatoxins at the evidence-supported compound-group level for Amanita phalloides and does not assert a complete composition, structure, dose, or outcome model.

title: Batrachotoxin
summary: Isolated alkaloid documented in Phyllobates terribilis skin. It is not a synonym for the organism's complete skin poison mixture.

title: Botulinum neurotoxin
summary: This isolated-toxin record describes the neurotoxin that causes botulism; it does not reclassify Clostridium botulinum as venomous.

title: Ricin
summary: This isolated-toxin record describes ricin as a toxic protein associated with castor bean seeds; it does not make dose, lethality, or exposure-route claims beyond the cited source.

title: Solenopsin A
summary: Featured representative compound. Not claimed as sole mediator of all clinical effects.
